Budget reconciliation isn’t about spreadsheets—it’s about realigning a bloated federal government with the priorities of hardworking Americans. Under President Trump’s leadership, this process delivered historic tax cuts and slashed bureaucratic waste. 

Now? D.C. insiders abuse it to fund foreign aid and green scams while ignoring border security and inflation. The Senate’s FY25 budget resolution claims fiscal discipline but hides loopholes for endless spending. 

Time to gut the swamp’s slush funds and force D.C. to serve taxpayers, not itself.

Work requirements for welfare aren’t just fiscal sanity—they’re moral clarity. The People CARE Act (H.R. 150) proves that streamlining bloated programs while incentivizing work lifts families out of dependency. GAO reports show $175B in annual overpayments across 71 federal programs—proof that unchecked handouts fuel waste, not prosperity. 

Biden-era policies poured billions into failed projects like incomplete EV stations and DEI grants abroad, while Trump’s DOGE clawed back $1.9B from bureaucratic slush funds. Tying aid to work aligns with the Iowa model that saved $217M by prioritizing accountability. Redirect those savings to veterans’ care and border security instead of funding ideological pet projects. 

Real compassion empowers self-reliance, not perpetual government dependence.
@RepArrington So you use GAO’s work but want to half their budget?

The SNAP program’s $10.5B in improper payments isn’t just bureaucratic failure—it’s systemic rot. The One Big Beautiful Bill Act (H.R.1) aims to slash this waste by tightening eligibility checks and ending state loopholes that enable fraud. GAO’s 2024 report confirms states routinely ignore basic verification, while LexisNexis data shows EBT skimming now costs $4.48 for every $1 stolen.

Baltimore’s $16M scheme and Florida’s identity theft ring aren’t outliers—they’re inevitable when D.C. prioritizes expanding benefits over securing them. Real reform means block-granting SNAP to states with strict anti-fraud mandates, auditing every dollar, and prosecuting bureaucrats who enable this theft.

No more blank checks for incompetence.
